==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Mockly&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Plugins/MocklyTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Mockly&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using Mockly;
using System.Net;

// Verify.Mockly: Snapshots a Mockly HttpMock and the requests it captured, instead of asserting on them one by one.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.Mockly
// Note: The HttpMock fluent API comes from the Mockly package; this plugin only teaches Verify how
// to write the results.
// Note: It covers the same ground as Verify.Http's MockHttpClient and Verify.Flurl's HttpTest, so
// one of the three is usually enough.
// Note: The only plugin here that targets net472.
public class MocklyTests
{
    // Verifying the mock writes every request it captured, with the method, host, path and
    // whether it matched an expectation, so one snapshot covers what would be several asserts.
    [Fact]
    public async Task GetRequest()
    {
        var mock = new HttpMock();

        mock.ForGet()
            .ForHttps()
            .ForHost("api.example.com")
            .WithPath("/api/users/123")
            .RespondsWithJsonContent(
                new
                {
                    id = 123,
                    name = "John"
                });

        var client = mock.GetClient();
        await client.GetAsync("https://api.example.com/api/users/123");
        await Verify(mock);
    }

    // CollectingRequestsIn narrows the snapshot to the requests one expectation matched, which
    // keeps unrelated traffic from the mock out of the verified file.
    [Fact]
    public async Task RequestCollection()
    {
        var mock = new HttpMock();
        var requests = new RequestCollection();

        mock.ForGet()
            .ForHttps()
            .ForHost("api.example.com")
            .WithPath("/api/users/*")
            .CollectingRequestsIn(requests)
            .RespondsWithJsonContent(
                new
                {
                    id = 1,
                    name = "John"
                });

        var client = mock.GetClient();
        await client.GetAsync("https://api.example.com/api/users/1");
        await client.GetAsync("https://api.example.com/api/users/2");
        await Verify(requests);
    }

    // A captured request body is a member like any other, so ScrubMember from Verify core
    // removes it when it carries a value that changes on every run.
    [Fact]
    public async Task ScrubBody()
    {
        var mock = new HttpMock();

        mock.ForPost()
            .ForHttps()
            .ForHost("api.example.com")
            .WithPath("/api/users")
            .RespondsWithStatus(HttpStatusCode.Created);

        var client = mock.GetClient();
        await client.PostAsync(
            "https://api.example.com/api/users",
            new StringContent("""{"name":"Jane"}"""));
        await Verify(mock)
            .ScrubMember("Body");
    }
}
